title.en: Volume 160 Biographies 48: Wang Zhang, Wei Yuan, Jin Lian, Shi Pu, Luo Tong, Luo Qi, Zhang Xuan, Zhang Peng, Li Yu
title.raw: 卷一百六十 列傳第四十八 王彰 魏源 金濂 石璞 羅通 羅綺 張瑄 張鵬 李裕 Volume 160 Biographies 48: Wang Zhang, Wei Yuan, Jin Lian, Shi Pu, Luo Tong, Luo Qi, Zhang Xuan, Zhang Peng, Li Yu

sentences.zh: 王彰 魏源 金濂 石璞 王巹 羅通 羅綺 張固 張瑄 張鵬 李裕

translations.literal: Wang Zhang, Wei Yuan, Jin Lian, Shi Pu, Wang Ji, Luo Tong, Luo Qi, Zhang Gu, Zhang Xuan, Zhang Peng, Li Yu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, Wei Yuan, Jin Lian, Shi Pu, Wang Ji, Luo Tong, Luo Qi, Zhang Gu, Zhang Xuan, Zhang Peng, and Li Yu

sentences.zh: 王彰，字文昭，鄭人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang, style name Wenzhao, was a native of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, whose style name was Wenzhao, came from Zheng.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年舉於鄉，補國子生。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he was nominated in the provincial examination and enrolled as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twentieth year of the Hongwu reign and entered the Imperial Academy as a student.

sentences.zh: 使山東平糴，以廉幹稱，擢吏科源士。

translations.literal: Sent to Shandong to stabilize grain purchases, he was praised for integrity and competence and was promoted to a yuanshi post in the Personnel Section of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: While on assignment in Shandong to stabilize grain purchases, he won a reputation for integrity and ability and was promoted to a junior post in the Personnel Section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 逾年，革源士，改給事中，累遷山西左參政。

translations.literal: After a year the yuanshi post was abolished; he was made a supervising secretary and was promoted in stages to Left Vice Commissioner in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when the yuanshi post was abolished, he was appointed supervising secretary and eventually rose to become Left Vice Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年召為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongle reign he was called to the capital as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父喪，服除，改戶部。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; after the mourning period ended he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he completed the mourning period and was reassigned to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 陝西大疫，奉使祀西嶽。

translations.literal: When a great epidemic struck Shaanxi, he was sent on a mission to sacrifice at the Western Marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe epidemic in Shaanxi, he was dispatched on a mission to offer sacrifices at Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 新安民鬻子女償賦。

translations.literal: The people of Xin'an were selling their sons and daughters to pay taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In Xin'an, commoners were selling their children to pay off tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 彰奏為蠲除，贖還所鬻。

translations.literal: Zhang memorialized to have the levies remitted and to redeem those who had been sold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized for tax remission and had the sold children bought back and restored to their families.

sentences.zh: 改右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the post of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 陝西僉事馬英激肅州番為變，殺御史及都指揮。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Assistant Commissioner Ma Ying provoked the Subei tribes into rebellion, killing a censor and a regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ying, an assistant commissioner in Shaanxi, provoked the Subei tribes at Suzhou into revolt and killed a touring censor and the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 彰劾英，置極典。

translations.literal: Zhang impeached Ying and had him subjected to the severest penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang impeached Ma Ying and had him executed under the harshest statute.

sentences.zh: 又劾御史陳孟旭受賕枉法、文獻盜銀課、及金吾指揮李嚴逐母不養，皆坐死。

translations.literal: He also impeached the censor Chen Mengxu for taking bribes and perverting the law, Wen Xian for stealing silver from the tax levy, and the Jinyu Commander Li Yan for driving out his mother and refusing to support her; all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Censor Chen Mengxu for bribery and corruption, Wen Xian for embezzling silver from the tax levy, and Jinyu Guard Commander Li Yan for abandoning his mother without support; all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 他所論劾甚眾。

translations.literal: The persons he impeached and prosecuted were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His impeachments and prosecutions were numerous besides these.

sentences.zh: 十一年從帝北巡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor on the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor on the northern inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 彰有母年八十餘矣，命歸省，賜其母冠服金幣。

translations.literal: Zhang had a mother more than eighty years old; he was ordered to return home on leave and his mother was granted ceremonial cap and robe and gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's mother was more than eighty years old, so he was ordered home on leave and the court bestowed on her ceremonial dress, gold, and silk.

sentences.zh: 諭之曰：「君子居官不忘親，居家不忘君。

translations.literal: He was instructed, saying: A gentleman in office does not forget his parents; at home he does not forget his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "A gentleman in office must not forget his parents, and at home he must not forget his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 凡所過，民安否，吏賢不肖，悉以聞。

translations.literal: Everywhere you pass, whether the people are secure or not and whether officials are worthy or unworthy, report all of it."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever you go, report fully on whether the people are secure and which officials are capable or corrupt."

sentences.zh: 」彰還，奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: When Zhang returned, his memorials pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang returned and reported, his memorials met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 久之，進右都御史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十九年，帝遣廷臣二十六人巡撫天下，彰與給事中王勵往河南。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the emperor dispatched twenty-six court officials to tour and pacify the realm; Zhang and the supervising secretary Wang Li went to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor sent twenty-six court officials to serve as grand coordinators throughout the empire; Zhang and Supervising Secretary Wang Li were assigned to Henan.

sentences.zh: 終明世，大臣得撫鄉土者，彰與葉春而已。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty, among great ministers who were allowed to administer their native places, only Zhang and Ye Chun did so.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Ming period, only Zhang and Ye Chun among senior ministers were permitted to oversee their home regions.

sentences.zh: 河南水災，民多流亡，長吏不加恤。

translations.literal: Henan suffered flooding; many people fled as refugees, and the chief officials showed them no relief.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck Henan, large numbers of people became refugees, yet the local authorities offered them little relief.

sentences.zh: 彰奏黜貪刻者百餘人，罷不急之征十餘事。

translations.literal: Zhang memorialized to dismiss more than a hundred greedy and harsh officials and to abolish more than ten levies that were not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized for the dismissal of more than a hundred corrupt and harsh officials and for the repeal of more than ten nonessential levies.

sentences.zh: 招復流民，發廩振貸，多所全活。

translations.literal: He summoned back the displaced people, opened granaries for relief loans, and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled refugees, opened granaries for relief grain and loans, and thereby saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 還朝，命督餉北征。

translations.literal: On his return to court he was ordered to supervise provisions for the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned to court, he was ordered to supervise grain supplies for the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，河溢開封，命彰與都指揮李信往振恤。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, the Yellow River overflowed at Kaifeng; Zhang and the regional commander Li Xin were ordered to go and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, the Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng, and Zhang was sent with Regional Commander Li Xin to provide disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年五月，命彰自良鄉抵南京巡撫軍民。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Xuande he was ordered to tour and pacify troops and civilians from Liangxiang to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Xuande he was ordered to oversee troops and civilians from Liangxiang south to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋以所言率常事，降敕切責，令詳具利病以聞。

translations.literal: Soon, because what he reported was mostly routine matters, an edict was issued sternly rebuking him and ordering him to set forth benefits and harms in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because his reports were largely routine, the emperor issued a stern edict rebuking him and ordering detailed accounts of what helped or harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 復諭侍臣曰：「兩京相距數千里，驛使往來為擾，或遘水旱，小民失所，朝使還及御史巡曆皆不以告，故遣彰往視。

translations.literal: He again instructed the attending ministers, saying: The two capitals are several thousand li apart; courier traffic back and forth is a nuisance. When flood or drought occurs and common people lose their livelihoods, returning envoys and touring censors do not report it, so Zhang was sent to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: He also told his close ministers: "The two capitals lie thousands of li apart, and constant courier traffic is a burden. When floods or drought strike and commoners lose their livelihoods, returning envoys and touring censors report nothing, which is why I sent Zhang to look into conditions.

sentences.zh: 今所奏多細故。

translations.literal: What he has now memorialized is mostly petty matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what he has reported is mostly petty detail.

sentences.zh: 大臣如此，朕復何望！

translations.literal: When a great minister is like this, what more can I hope for!
translations.idiomatic: When a senior minister behaves like this, what can I still expect!

sentences.zh: 卿等當悉朕意，君臣同體，勿有所疑。

translations.literal: You ought all to understand my intent; ruler and ministers are one body—have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: You must all understand my intent: ruler and ministers share one body, and you should harbor no doubts."

sentences.zh: 」尋召還，命與都督山雲巡山海至居庸諸關隘。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and ordered, together with the regional commander Shan Yun, to inspect the passes from Shanhai to Juyong and the other frontier barriers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and ordered, together with Regional Commander Shan Yun, to inspect the frontier passes from Shanhaiguan through Juyong and the other garrisons.

sentences.zh: 逾二月還，奏將士擅離者，帝命逮治。

translations.literal: After more than two months he returned and memorialized on officers and soldiers who had left their posts without authorization; the emperor ordered them arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: After more than two months he returned, reported officers and men who had deserted their posts, and the emperor ordered them arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 遂命兵部三月一遣御史、給事中點閱。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of War was ordered every three months to dispatch censors and supervising secretaries to inspect and review.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War was then ordered to send censors and supervising secretaries every three months for inspection.

sentences.zh: 明年四月卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office the following fourth month.

sentences.zh: 彰嚴介自持，請托皆絕，然用法過刻。

translations.literal: Zhang was stern and upright in his self-conduct and rejected all private requests, yet he applied the law with excessive severity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was stern and upright and refused all private solicitations, yet he applied the law with excessive harshness.

sentences.zh: 其母屢以為言，不能改。

translations.literal: His mother repeatedly spoke to him about this, but he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: His mother admonished him repeatedly, but he could not change his ways.

sentences.zh: 時劉觀為左都御史。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Guan was Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Guan served as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 人謂「彰公而不恕，觀私而不刻」雲。

translations.literal: People said, "Zhang is fair but not forgiving; Guan is partial but not harsh," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: People said of them: "Zhang is fair but unforgiving; Guan is partial but not harsh."

sentences.zh: 魏源，字文淵，建昌縣人。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan, style name Wenyuan, was a native of Jianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan, whose style name was Wenyuan, came from Jianchang County.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 除監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 辨松江知府黃子威誣。

translations.literal: He cleared the false charge against Huang Ziwei, prefect of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared Prefect Huang Ziwei of Songjiang from a false accusation.

sentences.zh: 奏減浙東瀕海漁課。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the coastal fishing levy in eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a reduction of the coastal fishing tax in eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 巡按陝西。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as touring inspector of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 西安大疫，療活甚眾。

translations.literal: When a great epidemic struck Xi'an, he treated and saved very many people.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe epidemic in Xi'an, he treated the sick and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「諸府倉粟積一千九十余萬石，足支十年。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: The granaries of the various prefectures hold more than 1,900,000 shi of grain, enough to last ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The prefectural granaries hold more than 1,900,000 shi of grain, enough to supply the region for ten years.

sentences.zh: 今民疫妨農，請輸鈔代兩稅之半。

translations.literal: Now the people's epidemic hampers farming; I request that paper money be paid in place of half the two taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Because the epidemic is hindering farming, I ask that paper money be accepted in lieu of half the land and labor taxes."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 涼州土寇將為變。

translations.literal: Bandits among the native communities of Liangzhou were about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits in Liangzhou were on the verge of revolt.

sentences.zh: 亟請剿，亂遂息。

translations.literal: He urgently requested a punitive campaign, and the disturbance was soon quelled.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently requested a punitive expedition, and the unrest was quickly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 兩遭喪，俱起復。

translations.literal: He twice suffered bereavement and on both occasions was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He twice left office for mourning and on both occasions was recalled before the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年出為浙江按察副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he went out to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi he was posted as Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年召署刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he was summoned to act as Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he was summoned to serve as acting Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 五年，河南旱荒，民多轉徙。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Henan suffered drought and famine, and many people migrated away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year drought and famine struck Henan, and large numbers of people migrated elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 帝以源廉正有為，命為左布政使，俾馳驛之任。

translations.literal: Because the emperor regarded Yuan as incorrupt, upright, and capable, he was appointed Left Administrative Commissioner and ordered to take up the post by urgent courier relay.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yuan as incorrupt, upright, and effective, the emperor appointed him Left Administrative Commissioner and ordered him to take up the post by express relay.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎許廓往撫輯，廷議又起丁憂布政使李昌祺原官。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister Xu Kuo was sent to pacify and settle the region, and the court debated reinstating Li Changqi, the administrative commissioner in mourning, to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Kuo was then sent to pacify the region, while court debate also turned on reinstating Li Changqi, the administrative commissioner then in mourning, to his former post.

sentences.zh: 源與廓、昌祺發倉廩，免逋賦雜役，流民漸歸。

translations.literal: Yuan, together with Kuo and Changqi, opened granaries, remitted overdue taxes and miscellaneous corvée levies, and the displaced people gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, together with Xu Kuo and Li Changqi, opened granaries, remitted tax arrears and miscellaneous levies, and refugees gradually returned home.

sentences.zh: 雨亦旋降，歲大豐。

translations.literal: Rain soon fell as well, and the year was greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Rain soon followed, and the year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 居三年，召還，授刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was recalled and appointed Left Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was recalled and appointed Left Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年，永豐民夏九旭等據大盤山為亂。

translations.literal: The following year the people of Yongfeng, Xia Jiuxu and others, seized Dapan Mountain and rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xia Jiuxu and others among the people of Yongfeng seized Dapan Mountain and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝以源江西人，命撫之，都督任禮帥兵隨其後。

translations.literal: Because Yuan was a man of Jiangxi, the emperor ordered him to pacify the rebels, with the regional commander Ren Li leading troops behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan was a native of Jiangxi, the emperor ordered him to pacify the rebels while Regional Commander Ren Li led troops in support.

sentences.zh: 未至，官軍擒九旭，因命二人采木四川，兼飭邊務。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, government troops captured Jiuxu; the two men were therefore ordered to procure timber in Sichuan and also to oversee frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, government forces had already captured Jiuxu, so both men were ordered to procure timber in Sichuan and also to oversee frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，錄上疑獄，且請推行於天下，報可。

translations.literal: In a year of drought he recorded doubtful cases and memorialized that the practice be extended throughout the realm; the reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year he submitted a register of doubtful cases and asked that the practice be extended empire-wide; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 旋坐決獄不當，與侍郎何文淵俱下獄。

translations.literal: Soon he was convicted of improper judgment in cases and was imprisoned together with Vice Minister He Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon imprisoned together with Vice Minister He Wenyuan for improper judgments in criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 得宥，復以上遼王貴烚罪狀，不言其內亂事，與三司官皆系詔獄。

translations.literal: He was pardoned, but again, because in reporting the crimes of the Prince of Liaodong, Gui Juan, he did not mention his internal rebellion, he and the officials of the three offices were all imprisoned by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned, but was imprisoned again together with the three-commission officials because, in reporting the crimes of Prince Gui Juan of Liaodong, he had failed to mention the prince's internal rebellion.

sentences.zh: 累月，釋還職。

translations.literal: After several months they were released and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After several months they were released and restored to their posts.

sentences.zh: 源在刑部久，議獄多平恕。

translations.literal: Yuan served long in the Ministry of Justice, and in deliberating cases he was mostly lenient and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served for a long time in the Ministry of Justice and generally favored lenient judgments.

sentences.zh: 陝西僉事計資言，武臣雜犯等罪，予半俸，謫極邊。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Assistant Commissioner Ji Zi proposed that for miscellaneous offenses by military officers and the like, half salary be granted and exile to the farthest frontier imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zi, an assistant commissioner in Shaanxi, proposed that for miscellaneous offenses by military officers, offenders receive half pay and be banished to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 源以所言深刻，奏寢之。

translations.literal: Yuan regarded the proposal as excessively harsh and memorialized to have it shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan regarded the proposal as excessively harsh and memorialized to have it tabled.

sentences.zh: 郎中林厚言禁刁訟、告訐及擇理刑官、勘重囚務憑贓具四事，皆以源議得施行。

translations.literal: The director Lin Hou proposed four measures: banning vexatious litigation and denunciation, selecting officials for criminal justice, and requiring that serious prisoners be investigated strictly according to evidence of stolen goods; all were adopted through Yuan's deliberation and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Director Lin Hou proposed four measures—banning vexatious suits and malicious accusations, selecting qualified criminal judges, and requiring that serious cases be investigated strictly on the basis of physical evidence—and all were adopted and implemented on Yuan's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 六年以足疾命朝朔望。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of illness in his feet, he was ordered to attend court only on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, because of a foot ailment, he was ordered to attend court only on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 八年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he retired and soon died.

sentences.zh: 金濂，字宗瀚，山陽人。

translations.literal: Jin Lian, style name Zonghan, was a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian, whose style name was Zonghan, came from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂十六年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Yongle and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Yongle and was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，巡按廣東，廉能最。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande he toured and inspected Guangdong and was ranked highest for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he toured Guangdong and was ranked foremost for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 改按江西、浙江。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tour Jiangxi and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to tour Jiangxi and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 捕巨盜不獲，坐免。

translations.literal: He failed to capture a great bandit and was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed to capture a major bandit, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 盜就執，乃復官。

translations.literal: When the bandit was captured, he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandit was captured, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 嘗言郡縣吏貪濁，宜敕按察司、巡按御史察廉能者，如洪武間故事，遣使勞賚，則清濁分，循良勸。

translations.literal: He once said that prefectural and county officials were greedy and corrupt, and that the Surveillance Commission and touring censors ought to be ordered to identify the incorrupt and capable, as in the Hongwu precedent, and send envoys to reward them with gifts; then the pure and the corrupt would be distinguished and the worthy encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that because prefectural and county officials were often corrupt, the Surveillance Commission and touring censors should identify the upright and capable, as in the Hongwu precedent, and send envoys to reward them; thus the worthy and the corrupt would be distinguished and good governance encouraged.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 用薦遷陝西副使。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was transferred to Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted to Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年秋拜刑部尚書，侍經筵。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Justice and attended the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Justice and attended the imperial Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 十一年，安鄉伯張安與弟爭祿，詔逮治。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Earl of Anxiang, Zhang An, disputed his stipend with his younger brother; an edict ordered them arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Earl Zhang An of Anxiang disputed his stipend with his younger brother, and an edict ordered both men arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 法司與戶部相諉，言官劾濂及戶部尚書王佐，右都御史陳鎰，侍郎丁鉉、馬昂，副都御史丁璿、程富等，俱下獄。

translations.literal: The judicial offices and the Ministry of Revenue shifted blame onto each other; remonstrating officials impeached Lian and Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo, Right Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi, Vice Ministers Ding Xian and Ma Ang, Vice Censors-in-Chief Ding Xuan and Cheng Fu, and others; all were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices and the Ministry of Revenue blamed each other; remonstrating officials impeached Jin Lian along with Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo, Right Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi, Vice Ministers Ding Xian and Ma Ang, and Vice Censors-in-Chief Ding Xuan and Cheng Fu; all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 數日，釋之。

translations.literal: After several days they were released.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they were released.

sentences.zh: 福建賊鄧茂七等為亂，都督劉聚、都御史張楷征之，不克。

translations.literal: The bandits of Fujian, Deng Maoqi and others, rose in rebellion; the regional commander Liu Ju and the Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kai campaigned against them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Maoqi and other rebels in Fujian rose in revolt; Regional Commander Liu Ju and Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kai campaigned against them without success.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月大發兵，命甯陽侯陳懋等為將軍往討，以濂參軍務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year a great force was mobilized; the Marquis of Ningyang, Chen Mao, and others were appointed generals to go and suppress them, with Lian assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year the court mobilized a large army, appointed Marquis Chen Mao of Ningyang and others as generals to suppress the rebels, and assigned Jin Lian to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 比至，御史丁瑄已大破賊。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, the censor Ding Xuan had already inflicted a great defeat on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, Censor Ding Xuan had already inflicted a major defeat on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 茂七死，餘賊擁其兄子伯孫據九龍山，拒官軍。

translations.literal: Maoqi died; the remaining rebels supported his elder brother's son Bosun, who held Jiulong Mountain and resisted the government army.
translations.idiomatic: After Maoqi died, the remaining rebels rallied behind his elder brother's son Bosun, who held Jiulong Mountain and resisted government forces.

sentences.zh: 濂與眾謀，羸師誘之出，伏精兵，入其壘，遂擒伯孫。

translations.literal: Lian discussed with the others a plan to display a weakened force and lure them out, then set elite troops in ambush, enter their stronghold, and thereby capture Bosun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian and the commanders devised a plan to feign weakness and lure the rebels out, then ambush them with elite troops, storm their stronghold, and capture Bosun.

sentences.zh: 帝乃移楷討浙寇，而留濂擊平餘賊未下者。

translations.literal: The emperor then transferred Kai to suppress the bandits of Zhejiang and left Lian to attack and pacify the remaining rebels not yet subdued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then transferred Zhang Kai to suppress bandits in Zhejiang and left Jin Lian to finish off the remaining unrebelled forces.

sentences.zh: 會英宗北狩，兵事棘，召還。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Yingzong went north on campaign and military affairs became urgent; Lian was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong went north on campaign and was captured at Tumu, the military crisis became acute and Jin Lian was recalled.

sentences.zh: 言者交劾濂無功，景帝不問，加濂太子賓客，給二俸。

translations.literal: Critics repeatedly impeached Lian for achieving nothing; Emperor Jingdi paid no heed and added for Lian the post of Household Companion of the Heir Apparent, granting two salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Critics repeatedly impeached Jin Lian for achieving nothing, but Emperor Jingdi ignored the charges, appointed him Household Companion of the Heir Apparent, and granted him double salary.

sentences.zh: 尋改戶部尚書，進太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Minister of Revenue and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時四方用兵，需餉急，濂綜核無遺，議上撙節便宜十六事，國用得無乏。

translations.literal: At the time campaigns were being fought on all sides and supplies were urgently needed; Lian audited accounts without omission and proposed sixteen measures of frugality and expedient economy, so that state revenue was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With campaigns on every front and supplies urgently needed, Jin Lian audited accounts exhaustively and proposed sixteen measures of frugality and practical economy, so that state finances did not run short.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上皇還。

translations.literal: Before long the former emperor returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the former emperor returned from captivity.

sentences.zh: 也先請遣使往來如初，帝堅意絕之。

translations.literal: Esen requested that envoys be sent back and forth as before; the emperor firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Esen asked to restore diplomatic exchanges as before, but the emperor firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 濂再疏諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Lian memorialized again in remonstrance, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian memorialized again in protest, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位，詔免景泰二年天下租十之三。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor took the throne, an edict exempted one-third of the realm's rents for the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, he issued an edict exempting one-third of the empire's land tax for the second year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 濂檄有司，但減米麥，其折收銀布絲帛者征如故。

translations.literal: Lian issued orders to the officials to reduce only rice and wheat grain; taxes collected in converted silver, cloth, silk, and silk fabrics were levied as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian ordered local officials to reduce only grain taxes in rice and wheat, while silver, cloth, silk, and fabric levies collected in commutation were exacted as before.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，學士江淵以為言，命部查理。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Academician Jiang Yuan raised the matter, and the emperor ordered the ministries to investigate and rectify it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, Academician Jiang Yuan reported the matter, and the emperor ordered the ministries to investigate.

sentences.zh: 濂內慚，抵無有。

translations.literal: Lian was inwardly ashamed but denied that anything was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian was inwardly ashamed but denied any wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 給事中李侃等請詰天下有司違詔故。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Li Kan and others requested that officials throughout the realm who had violated the edict be called to account.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Li Kan and others asked that officials throughout the empire who had violated the edict be investigated.

sentences.zh: 濂恐事敗，乃言：「銀布絲帛，詔書未載，若概減免，國用何資？

translations.literal: Lian feared the affair would be exposed and therefore said: "Silver, cloth, and silk fabrics were not mentioned in the edict; if they were all reduced or exempted, how would state revenue be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Jin Lian argued: "Silver, cloth, and silk were not mentioned in the edict; if all were reduced, how would the state meet its expenses?

sentences.zh: 」於是給事中御史劾濂失信於民，為國斂怨，且訐其陰事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the supervising secretaries and censors impeached Lian for breaking faith with the people, amassing resentment for the state, and also denounced his secret misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors then impeached Jin Lian for breaking faith with the people, stirring public resentment, and denounced his private misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝欲宥之，而侃與御史王允力爭，遂下都察院獄。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to pardon him, but Kan and Censor Wang Yun argued forcefully, and he was therefore sent to the Censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to pardon him, but Li Kan and Censor Wang Yun argued forcefully, and he was sent to the Censorate prison.

sentences.zh: 越三日釋之，削宮保，改工部。

translations.literal: After three days he was released, stripped of his Grand Guardian title, and transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he was released, stripped of his Grand Guardian title, and transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書何文淵言理財非濂不可，乃復還戶部。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan said that no one but Lian could manage finances, so he was restored to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan said finances could not be managed without Jin Lian, so he was restored to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 濂上疏自理，遂乞骸骨，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Lian memorialized in his own defense and then requested retirement; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian memorialized in self-defense and then requested retirement; the emperor comforted him and kept him at his post.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，復宮保。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, his Grand Guardian title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was formally established, his Grand Guardian title was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋復條上節軍匠及僧道冗食共十事。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized again with ten items on economizing military artisans and redundant clergy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized again with ten proposals to economize on military artisans and redundant Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 五年卒官，以軍功追封沭陽伯，諡榮襄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office; for military merit he was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Shuyang with the posthumous name Rongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office; for military merit he was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Shuyang with the posthumous title Rongxiang.

sentences.zh: 濂剛果有才，所至以嚴辦稱，然接下多暴怒。

translations.literal: Lian was resolute, capable, and talented; wherever he served he was known for strict handling, yet he was often violent and angry toward subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lian was resolute and talented; wherever he served he was known for strict administration, yet he was often violent and angry with subordinates.

sentences.zh: 在刑部持法稍深。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Justice he applied the law rather severely.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Ministry of Justice he applied the law with some severity.

sentences.zh: 及為戶部，值兵興財詘，頗厚斂以足用雲。

translations.literal: When he served in the Ministry of Revenue, campaigns were underway and finances were strained; he collected rather heavily to make ends meet, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Revenue during wartime financial strain, he is said to have collected rather heavily to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 石璞，字仲玉，臨漳人。

translations.literal: Shi Pu, style name Zhongyu, was a native of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, whose style name was Zhongyu, came from Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年舉於鄉，入國學。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle he was nominated in the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongle he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 選授御史。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 正統初，歷任江西按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he served in succession as Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign he served as Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 三年坐逸囚，降副使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was demoted to vice commissioner because a prisoner escaped on his watch.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was demoted to vice commissioner after a prisoner escaped under his supervision.

sentences.zh: 璞善斷疑獄。

translations.literal: Pu was skilled at deciding doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu was skilled at resolving doubtful criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 民娶婦，三日歸寧，失之。

translations.literal: A commoner took a wife; on the third day she went home to visit her parents and disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: A man took a wife; on the third day she returned to her parents' home for a visit and vanished.

sentences.zh: 婦翁訟婿殺女，誣服論死。

translations.literal: The wife's father sued the son-in-law for killing his daughter; the son-in-law falsely confessed and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Her father sued the son-in-law for murder; the son-in-law falsely confessed and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 璞禱於神，夢神示以麥字。

translations.literal: Pu prayed to the gods and dreamed that a deity showed him the character mai (wheat).
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu prayed to the gods and dreamed that a deity showed him the character mai (wheat).

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「麥者，兩人夾一人也。

translations.literal: Pu said: "Mai means two people flanking one person.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu said: "Mai means two people flanking one person.

sentences.zh: 」比明，械囚趣行刑。

translations.literal: At daybreak he had the prisoner shackled and hurried to execution.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he had the prisoner shackled and hurried toward execution.

sentences.zh: 未出，一童子窺門屏間。

translations.literal: Before they went out, a boy was peeping through the door screen.
translations.idiomatic: Before they left, a boy was peeping through the door screen.

sentences.zh: 捕入，則道士徒也。

translations.literal: They seized him—it was a Daoist novice.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him; he was a Daoist novice.

sentences.zh: 叱曰：「爾師令爾偵事乎？

translations.literal: He shouted: "Did your master send you to spy?
translations.idiomatic: He shouted: "Did your master send you to spy on us?

sentences.zh: 」童子首實，果二道士匿婦槁麥中。

translations.literal: The boy confessed at once; sure enough two Daoists had hidden the woman in a wheat straw stack.
translations.idiomatic: The boy confessed at once; two Daoists had indeed hidden the woman in a stack of wheat straw.

sentences.zh: 立捕，論如法。

translations.literal: They were immediately captured and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: They were immediately captured and sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 在江西數年，風紀整肅，雖婦豎無不知石憲使者。

translations.literal: After several years in Jiangxi, discipline was sternly maintained, so that even women and children knew Commissioner Shi of the Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in Jiangxi, discipline was so strict that even women and children knew Surveillance Commissioner Shi.

sentences.zh: 七年遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，以朝廷歲用物料，有司科派擾民，請於折糧銀內歲存千兩，令官買辦，庶官用可完，民亦不擾。

translations.literal: The next year, because the court's annual use of materials led local offices to impose extra levies that harassed the people, he requested that 1,000 taels be set aside each year from commuted grain silver for official purchase, so that government needs could be met without troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, because the court's annual material needs led local offices to impose levies that harassed the people, he asked that 1,000 taels be set aside yearly from commuted grain silver for official purchases, so government needs could be met without burdening the populace.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書王巹以不能屈意王振，十三年致仕去。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Ji could not defer to Wang Zhen and retired in the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Ji, unable to defer to Wang Zhen, retired in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 璞為振所善，遂召為尚書。

translations.literal: Pu was favored by Zhen and was therefore summoned as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, favored by Wang Zhen, was summoned to serve as minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，處州賊葉宗留作亂，總兵官徐恭等往討，以璞參其軍事。

translations.literal: The next year the bandit Ye Zongliu rebelled in Chuzhou; Regional Commander Xu Gong and others went to suppress him, with Pu assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the bandit Ye Zongliu rebelled in Chuzhou; Regional Commander Xu Gong and others campaigned against him, with Shi Pu assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 師未至，宗留已為其党陳鑒胡所殺。

translations.literal: Before the army arrived, Zongliu had already been killed by his follower Chen Jianhu.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived, Zongliu had already been killed by his follower Chen Jianhu.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張驥招降鑒胡，賊勢稍息。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Ji induced Jianhu to surrender, and the bandit strength gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Ji induced Chen Jianhu to surrender, and the rebellion gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 璞等逗遛無功，為御史張洪等所劾，詔俟師旋以聞。

translations.literal: Pu and the others dallied without achievement and were impeached by Censor Zhang Hong and others; an edict ordered them to report after the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu and the others dallied without success and were impeached by Censor Zhang Hong and others; an edict ordered them to report after the army returned.

sentences.zh: 已而景帝嗣位，召還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Jingdi succeeded to the throne and recalled them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Jingdi succeeded to the throne and recalled them.

sentences.zh: 論功，兼大理寺卿。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, he was concurrently appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was assessed, he was concurrently appointed chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 尋出募天下義勇，還朝。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to recruit volunteer troops throughout the realm and then returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went out to recruit volunteer troops throughout the empire and then returned to court.

sentences.zh: 會中官金英下獄，法司劾璞嘗賂英，遂並下璞獄，當斬，特宥之。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Jin Ying was imprisoned, the judicial offices impeached Pu for having bribed Ying; Pu was also imprisoned and sentenced to death, but was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Jin Ying was imprisoned, the judicial offices impeached Shi Pu for bribing him; Pu was imprisoned and sentenced to death but was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 出理大同軍餉。

translations.literal: He went out to administer military provisions at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to administer military provisions at Datong.

sentences.zh: 敵犯馬營，命提督宣府軍務。

translations.literal: The enemy invaded Maying, and he was ordered to supervise military affairs at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raided Maying, he was ordered to supervise military affairs at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 至則寇已退，還理部事。

translations.literal: When he arrived the bandits had already retreated, and he returned to handle ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the enemy had already withdrawn, and he returned to handle ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，給二俸。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted two salaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted double salary.

sentences.zh: 河決沙灣，命治之。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Shawan, and he was ordered to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Shawan, he was ordered to remedy the flood.

sentences.zh: 璞以決口未易塞，別浚渠。

translations.literal: Pu judged that the breach was not easy to block and therefore dug a separate channel.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu judged the breach difficult to seal and instead dug a separate channel.

sentences.zh: 自黑洋山至徐州，以通漕艘，而決口如故。

translations.literal: From Heiyang Mountain to Xuzhou, to open passage for grain transport vessels, while the breach remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: From Heiyang Mountain to Xuzhou he opened a channel for grain transport, while the breach remained unsealed.

sentences.zh: 乃命內官黎賢等偕御史彭誼助之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eunuch Li Xian and others, together with Censor Peng Yi, were ordered to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the eunuch Li Xian and others, together with Censor Peng Yi, to assist him.

sentences.zh: 于沙灣築石堤以禦決河，開月河二，引水益運河以殺水勢，決乃塞。

translations.literal: At Shawan they built stone dikes to hold back the broken river, opened two crescent canals, and diverted water to augment the Grand Canal to reduce the flood force; then the breach was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shawan they built stone dikes against the broken river, opened two crescent canals, and diverted water into the Grand Canal to reduce the flood force until the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 璞還言：「京師盜賊多出軍伍。

translations.literal: When Pu returned he reported: "Most thieves in the capital come from the military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Shi Pu reported: "Most thieves in the capital come from the military ranks.

sentences.zh: 間有獲者，輒雲『糧餉虧減，妻孥饑凍故』。

translations.literal: When some were captured, they would always say, 'Because provisions were reduced and wives and children were starving and freezing.'
translations.idiomatic: When some were captured, they would say, 'Our provisions were cut and our wives and children were starving and freezing.'

sentences.zh: 又聞兩畿、山東、河南被災窮民多事剽掠，不及今拊循，恐方來之憂甚于邊患。

translations.literal: He also heard that in the two capitals regions, Shandong, and Henan, many destitute people affected by disasters had turned to plunder; if they were not comforted now, he feared coming troubles would exceed border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that in the capital regions, Shandong, and Henan, many disaster-stricken poor had turned to plunder; unless comforted now, he feared domestic troubles would exceed border threats.

sentences.zh: 口外守軍，夜行晝伏，艱苦萬狀。

translations.literal: Frontier garrison troops outside the passes traveled by night and hid by day, suffering hardships beyond description.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops beyond the passes traveled by night and hid by day in hardships beyond description.

sentences.zh: 今邊疆未靖，宜增餉以作士氣，乃反減其月糧，此實啟盜誤國之端，非節財足用之術。

translations.literal: Now the frontier is not yet pacified; provisions ought to be increased to raise morale, yet monthly rations were instead reduced—this truly opens the door to banditry and harms the state; it is not a method of economizing to make ends meet.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier still unsettled, rations ought to be increased to raise morale, yet monthly grain was reduced—this truly invites banditry and harms the state; it is no way to economize effectively.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 沙灣復決，璞再往治之。

translations.literal: Shawan burst again, and Pu went again to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shawan burst again, Shi Pu went again to remedy it.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸，起復。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning and was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother and was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 王巹，郿人。

translations.literal: Wang Ji was a native of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji came from Mei.

sentences.zh: 永樂中鄉薦，曆山東左布政使，所至有惠政。

translations.literal: During Yongle he was nominated in the provincial examination and served as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shandong; wherever he served he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle he passed the provincial examination and served as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shandong, earning a reputation for benevolent governance wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 正統六年入為工部侍郎，代吳中為尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Works and replaced Wu Zhong as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Works and replaced Wu Zhong as Minister.

sentences.zh: 歸家十五年卒。

translations.literal: After returning home he died fifteen years later.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died fifteen years later.

sentences.zh: 羅通，字學古，吉水人。

translations.literal: Luo Tong, style name Xuegu, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong, whose style name was Xuegu, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the tenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the tenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 授御史，巡按四川。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and toured Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor and toured Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 都指揮郭贇與清軍御史汪琳中交通為奸利，通劾奏，逮治之。

translations.literal: The regional commander Guo Yun and the troop-clearing censor Wang Linzhong engaged in corrupt dealings for profit; Tong impeached them and had them arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Guo Yun and troop-clearing Censor Wang Linzhong engaged in corrupt dealings; Luo Tong impeached them and had them arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 三殿災，偕同官何忠等極陳時政闕失。

translations.literal: When the three main halls burned, he joined his colleagues He Zhong and others in strongly stating the failures of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the three main palace halls burned, he joined colleagues such as He Zhong in strongly criticizing current policy failures.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，出為交阯清化知州。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was sent out as prefect of Qinghua in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the emperor and was posted as prefect of Qinghua in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 正統初，遷兵部郎中，從尚書王驥整飭甘肅邊務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was transferred to director in the Ministry of War and followed Minister Wang Ji in reorganizing Gansu frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong he was transferred to director in the Ministry of War and followed Minister Wang Ji in reorganizing the Gansu frontier.

sentences.zh: 從破敵于兀魯乃還，以貪淫事為驥所覺。

translations.literal: After returning from defeating the enemy at Wulunai, his greed and licentious conduct were discovered by Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from defeating the enemy at Wulunai, his greed and licentious conduct were discovered by Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 驥遣通奏邊情，即疏通罪。

translations.literal: Ji sent Tong to memorialize on frontier conditions and at once exposed his own crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji sent Luo Tong to memorialize on frontier conditions and at once exposed Tong's own crimes.

sentences.zh: 下獄，謫廣西容山閘官。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned and demoted to gate officer at Rongshan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned and demoted to gate officer at Rongshan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 已，調東莞河泊所官。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to officer of the Dongguan River Depot.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to officer of the Dongguan River Depot.

sentences.zh: 九年，都督僉事曹儉薦其有文武才，乞收用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Regional Commander Cao Jian recommended that he had both civil and military talent and requested his employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Regional Commander Cao Jian recommended him for civil and military talent and asked that he be employed.

sentences.zh: 吏部執不可。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel insisted that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel refused.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年召還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 時楊洪督京營，命通參軍務兼理院事。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Hong supervised the capital army; Tong was ordered to assist in military affairs and concurrently handle court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yang Hong supervised the capital army; Luo Tong was ordered to assist in military affairs and concurrently handle court business.

sentences.zh: 言：「諸邊報警，率由守將畏徵調，飾詐以惑朝廷，遇賊數十輒稱殺敗數千。

translations.literal: He said: "Frontier alarms are mostly because garrison commanders fear being called up for campaigns and embellish reports to deceive the court; when they meet a few dozen bandits they claim to have killed or defeated thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Frontier alarms mostly arise because garrison commanders fear mobilization, embellish reports to deceive the court, and claim to have killed thousands when they meet only dozens of enemies.

sentences.zh: 向者德勝等門外不知斬馘幾何，而獲官者至六萬六千餘人。

translations.literal: Previously, outside Desheng Gate it was unknown how many heads were cut off, yet those who received promotions numbered more than 66,000 men.
translations.idiomatic: Previously outside Desheng Gate, no one knew how many enemy heads were taken, yet more than 66,000 men received promotions.

sentences.zh: 輦下且然，何況塞外。

translations.literal: If it is so even under the imperial carriage, how much more so beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: If this is so even at the capital, how much more so beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 且韓信起自行伍，穰苴拔於寒微，宜博搜將士中如信、苴者，與議軍事。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han Xin rose from the ranks and Rang Ju was chosen from humble origins; the court ought broadly to search among officers and soldiers for men like Xin and Ju and consult them on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han Xin rose from the ranks and Rang Ju was chosen from humble origins; the court ought to search broadly among officers and soldiers for men like them and consult them on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 若今腰玉珥貂，皆苟全性命保爵祿之人，憎賢忌才，能言而不能行，未足與議也。

translations.literal: As for those today who wear jade belts and ermine hats, they are all men who seek only to preserve their lives and salaries, who hate the worthy and envy talent, who can speak but cannot act—they are not fit to be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: As for those today who wear jade belts and ermine hats, they seek only to preserve their lives and salaries, hate the worthy and envy talent, and can speak but not act—they are unfit for consultation.

sentences.zh: 」意蓋詆謙與石亨輩。

translations.literal: His meaning was clearly aimed at denigrating Yu Qian and men such as Shi Heng.
translations.idiomatic: His meaning was clearly aimed at Yu Qian and men such as Shi Heng.

sentences.zh: 謙疏辨，言：「概責邊報不實，果有警，不奏必致誤事。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized in defense, saying: "To blame frontier reports in general as false—if there is a real alarm and it is not reported, that will certainly lead to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian memorialized in defense: "To blame frontier reports generally as false—if a real alarm goes unreported, disaster will certainly follow.

sentences.zh: 德勝門外官軍升級，惟武清侯石亨功次冊當先者萬九千八百餘人，及陣亡三千餘人而已，安所得六萬之多？

translations.literal: Outside Desheng Gate, among the officers and soldiers promoted, only 19,800-odd men ranked after Marquis Shi Heng of Wuqing on the merit register and the more than 3,000 who died in battle—how could there be as many as 60,000?
translations.idiomatic: Outside Desheng Gate, among those promoted, only 19,800-odd men ranked after Marquis Shi Heng of Wuqing on the merit register and the more than 3,000 killed in battle—whence 60,000?

sentences.zh: 通以為濫，宜將臣及亨等升爵削奪。

translations.literal: Tong regarded this as excessive and said that generals and Heng and the others ought to have their promotions and enfeoffments reduced or revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong regarded this as excessive and said generals and Heng and the others ought to have promotions and enfeoffments reduced or revoked.

sentences.zh: 有如韓信、穰苴者，乞即命指薦，並罷臣營務，俾專治部事。

translations.literal: If there are men like Han Xin and Rang Ju, I beg that they be named and recommended at once, and that my camp duties be ended so I may devote myself solely to ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If there are men like Han Xin and Rang Ju, I beg they be named and recommended at once, and that my camp duties end so I may devote myself to ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 」疏下廷議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down for court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 廷臣共言謙及石亨、楊洪實堪其任；

translations.literal: The court officials jointly said that Qian and Shi Heng and Yang Hong were truly equal to their tasks;
translations.idiomatic: Court officials jointly said Yu Qian, Shi Heng, and Yang Hong were truly equal to their tasks;

sentences.zh: 又謂通志在滅賊，無他。

translations.literal: they also said that Tong's aim was to destroy the bandits and that he had no other motive.
translations.idiomatic: they also said Luo Tong's aim was to destroy the enemy and that he had no other motive.

sentences.zh: 帝兩解之。

translations.literal: The emperor reconciled both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reconciled both sides.

sentences.zh: 尋敕謙錄功，不得如從前冒濫，蓋因通言而發也。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered Qian to record merit and not allow the former excessive inflation—this was issued because of Tong's words.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he ordered Yu Qian to record merit without the former excessive inflation—issued because of Luo Tong's words.

sentences.zh: 給事中覃浩等言通本以知兵用，不宜理院事，乃解其兼職。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Tan Hao and others said that Tong had originally been employed for his knowledge of military affairs and ought not to handle court affairs; he was therefore relieved of his concurrent post.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Tan Hao and others said Luo Tong had been employed for military knowledge and should not handle court affairs; his concurrent post was removed.

sentences.zh: 塞上軍民多為寇所掠。

translations.literal: On the frontier many soldiers and civilians were plundered by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier many soldiers and civilians were plundered by raiders.

sentences.zh: 通請榜諸邊能自歸者，軍免戍守三年，民復徭役終身。

translations.literal: Tong requested that proclamations be posted on all frontiers offering that those who surrendered of themselves should have soldiers exempted from garrison duty for three years and civilians restored to corvée service for life.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong asked that proclamations be posted on all frontiers offering that those who surrendered voluntarily would have soldiers exempted from garrison duty for three years and civilians restored to corvée for life.

sentences.zh: 又請懸封爵重賞，募能擒斬也先、伯顏帖木兒、喜甯者。

translations.literal: He also requested that sealed noble ranks and heavy rewards be posted, recruiting those who could capture and kill Esen, Bayan Temur, and Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that sealed noble ranks and heavy rewards be offered to anyone who could capture and kill Esen, Bayan Temur, and Xining.

sentences.zh: 已，又言：「古之將帥務搜拔眾才，如知山川形勢者可使導軍，能騰高越險者可使覘敵，能風角鳥占者可使備變。

translations.literal: Later he also said: "In antiquity generals and commanders strove to seek out and promote many talents—for example, those who knew mountains and rivers and terrain could be used to guide armies; those who could climb high and cross dangerous places could be used to spy on the enemy; those who could read winds and bird omens could be used to prepare for changes.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Ancient generals sought out many talents—those who knew terrain could guide armies, those who could climb and cross hazards could spy on the enemy, and those who read winds and birds could prepare for changes.

sentences.zh: 今軍中未見其人，乞敕廷臣各舉所知，命總兵官楊洪、副將孫鏜同臣考驗。

translations.literal: Today such men are not seen in the army; I beg that court officials each recommend those they know, and that the regional commander Yang Hong and the deputy commander Sun Yong together with me examine and test them.
translations.idiomatic: Today such men are not found in the army; I beg that court officials recommend those they know and that Regional Commander Yang Hong and Deputy Commander Sun Yong examine them with me.

sentences.zh: 」詔皆行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all these measures carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all these measures carried out.

sentences.zh: 宣府有警，總兵官硃謙告急。

translations.literal: There was an alarm at Xuanfu, and the regional commander Zhu Qian reported urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanfu reported an alarm, Regional Commander Zhu Qian sent an urgent report.

sentences.zh: 廷推都督同知范廣帥兵往，以通提督軍務。

translations.literal: The court recommended Vice Commissioner Fan Guang to lead troops there, with Tong supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court recommended Vice Commissioner Fan Guang to lead troops there, with Luo Tong supervising military affairs.

sentences.zh: 寇退，駐師懷來、宣府，以邊儲不敷，召還。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated, the army was stationed at Huailai and Xuanfu; because frontier stores were insufficient, they were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, the army remained at Huailai and Xuanfu; because frontier stores were insufficient, they were recalled.

sentences.zh: 六月，于謙以山西近寇，請遣大臣往鎮，楊洪亦乞遣重臣從雁門關護餉大同。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yu Qian, because Shanxi was near the bandits, requested that a great minister be sent to garrison it; Yang Hong also begged that a senior minister be sent through Yanmen Pass to escort provisions to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yu Qian, because Shanxi lay near the enemy, asked that a senior minister be sent to garrison it; Yang Hong also asked that a senior minister escort provisions to Datong through Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝以命通。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tong to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Luo Tong to go.

sentences.zh: 通不欲行，請得與謙、洪俱。

translations.literal: Tong did not wish to go and requested that he be allowed to go together with Qian and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong did not wish to go and asked to accompany Yu Qian and Yang Hong.

sentences.zh: 謙言國家多難，非臣子辭勞之日，奏乞躬往。

translations.literal: Qian said that the state faced many hardships and that this was not a time for subjects to decline labor; he memorialized begging to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian said the state faced many hardships and this was no time for subjects to shirk duty; he memorialized asking to go in person.

sentences.zh: 帝不允，卒命通。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent and ultimately ordered Tong to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ultimately ordered Luo Tong to go.

sentences.zh: 通本謙所舉，而每事牴牾，人由是不直通。

translations.literal: Tong had originally been recommended by Qian, yet on every matter he opposed him; people therefore did not approve of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong had originally been recommended by Yu Qian, yet opposed him on every matter; people therefore disapproved of Luo Tong.

sentences.zh: 二年召還，仍贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and again assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled and again assisted in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 東宮改建，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was rebuilt, he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent establishment was rebuilt, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上言：「貢使攜馬四萬餘匹，宜量增價酬之。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The tribute envoys are bringing more than 40,000 horses; the price paid for them ought to be increased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Tribute envoys are bringing more than 40,000 horses; their purchase price ought to be raised.

sentences.zh: 價增則後來益眾，此亦強中國弱外裔之一策。

translations.literal: If the price is raised, more will come later—this too is one method of strengthening China and weakening outer tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the price would bring more later—this too is a way to strengthen China and weaken outer tribes.

sentences.zh: 」帝以所貢馬率不堪用，若增價正墮賊計，寢通奏。

translations.literal: The emperor said that the horses presented were mostly unusable; if the price were raised it would fall into the enemy scheme, and Tong's memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the tribute horses were mostly unusable; raising the price would play into the enemy scheme, and Luo Tong's memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 四年進右都御史，贊軍務如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief while continuing to assist in military affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief while continuing to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 通好大言，遇人輒談兵。

translations.literal: Tong loved grand talk and whenever he met people would discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong loved grand talk and discussed military affairs whenever he met anyone.

sentences.zh: 自陳殺賊功，求世襲武職，為給事中王竑所劾。

translations.literal: He claimed credit for killing bandits himself and requested a hereditary military post; he was impeached by the supervising secretary Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed credit for killing bandits and requested a hereditary military post; Supervising Secretary Wang Hong impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝釋不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 天順初，自陳預謀迎駕，恐為石亨等所掩，乃授其二子所鎮撫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he claimed that he had beforehand plotted to welcome the emperor back and feared being overshadowed by men such as Shi Heng; he was therefore granted hereditary military posts to his two sons as garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshun he claimed he had plotted to welcome the emperor back and feared being overshadowed by Shi Heng and others; his two sons were therefore granted hereditary posts as garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 三年致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he retired.

sentences.zh: 成化六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chenghua he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬如例。

translations.literal: Imperial sacrifices and burial were granted according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sacrifices and burial were granted according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 羅綺，磁州人。

translations.literal: Luo Qi was a native of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi came from Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，授御史，按直隸、福建，有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he was appointed censor and toured Zhili and Fujian, gaining a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he was appointed censor and toured Zhili and Fujian, earning a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 正統九年參贊寧夏軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he assisted in Ningxia military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he assisted in Ningxia military affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾年當代，軍民詣鎮守都御史陳鎰乞留。

translations.literal: After a year his term was due to end, but soldiers and civilians went to the garrisoning Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi begging that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: After a year his term was due to end, but soldiers and civilians petitioned Garrisoning Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi to retain him.

sentences.zh: 以聞，命復任。

translations.literal: The matter was reported, and he was ordered to continue in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court was informed and ordered him to continue in office.

sentences.zh: 尋擢大理右寺丞，參贊如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review while continuing to assist as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review while continuing his assistant duties.

sentences.zh: 常以事劾指揮任信、陳斌。

translations.literal: He often impeached the commanders Ren Xin and Chen Bin on various matters.
translations.idiomatic: He often impeached Commanders Ren Xin and Chen Bin on various matters.

sentences.zh: 二人皆王振黨。

translations.literal: Both men were partisans of Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Both were partisans of Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，信、斌訐綺不法事，下總兵官黃真覆核。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, Xin and Bin denounced Qi for unlawful conduct; the matter was sent to Regional Commander Huang Zhen for review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, Ren Xin and Chen Bin denounced Luo Qi for misconduct; Regional Commander Huang Zhen was ordered to review the case.

sentences.zh: 真謂綺常詈宦官為「老奴」，以激怒振。

translations.literal: Zhen said that Qi often cursed eunuchs as old slaves, thereby angering Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhen reported that Luo Qi often cursed eunuchs as old slaves, angering Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 召還京。

translations.literal: Qi was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 法司擬贖，振改令錦衣衛再鞫。

translations.literal: The judicial offices proposed ransom, but Zhen changed the order to have the Embroidered-Uniform Guard interrogate again.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices proposed ransom, but Wang Zhen ordered the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to interrogate again.

sentences.zh: 指揮同知馬順鍛煉成獄，謫戍遼東。

translations.literal: Commander Ma Shun forged the case into a conviction, and Qi was banished to garrison the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Ma Shun fabricated the case into a conviction, and Luo Qi was banished to garrison the northeast.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，綺訴冤，不聽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi took the throne, Qi appealed his injustice, but the appeal was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi took the throne, Luo Qi appealed his injustice, but the appeal was denied.

sentences.zh: 尋用尚書于謙、金濂薦，召復故官，進右少卿，副李實使瓦剌。

translations.literal: Soon, on the recommendation of Ministers Yu Qian and Jin Lian, he was recalled to his former post, advanced to Right Vice Minister, and served as deputy to Li Shi on a mission to the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on the recommendation of Ministers Yu Qian and Jin Lian, he was recalled, promoted to Right Vice Minister, and served as deputy to Li Shi on a mission to the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 上皇還，以勞擢刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the former emperor returned, Qi was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Justice for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: When the former emperor returned, Luo Qi was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Justice for his service.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，出督雲南、四川軍儲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he went out to supervise military provisions in Yunnan and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he went out to supervise military provisions in Yunnan and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 已，代寇深鎮守松潘。

translations.literal: Later he replaced Kou Shen in garrisoning Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: He later replaced Kou Shen as garrison commander of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 賊首卓勞糾他寨阿兒結等頻為寇，綺擒斬之。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Zhuolao joined other stockades such as Aerjie in frequent raids; Qi captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chieftain Zhuolao joined other stockades such as Aerjie in frequent raids; Luo Qi captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 土官王永、高茂林、董敏相仇殺，守將不能制。

translations.literal: The native officials Wang Yong, Gao Maolin, and Dong Min were locked in mutual killing, and the garrison commanders could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Native officials Wang Yong, Gao Maolin, and Dong Min were locked in mutual killing, which garrison commanders could not control.

sentences.zh: 綺搗永巢誅之。

translations.literal: Qi destroyed Yong nest and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi destroyed Wang Yong stronghold and executed him.

sentences.zh: 又敗黑虎諸塞番，斬馘三百五十。

translations.literal: He also defeated the Black Tiger stockades and other tribes, cutting off 350 heads.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the Black Tiger stockades and other tribes, taking 350 heads.

sentences.zh: 在鎮七年，威名甚震。

translations.literal: After seven years in the garrison, his prestige was greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in the garrison, his prestige was greatly feared.

sentences.zh: 天順初，召為左副都御史，以功賜二品祿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and granted second-rank salary for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshun he was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and granted second-rank salary for merit.

sentences.zh: 御史張鵬、楊瑄劾石亨。

translations.literal: The censors Zhang Peng and Yang Xuan impeached Shi Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhang Peng and Yang Xuan impeached Shi Heng.

sentences.zh: 亨謂綺與右都御史耿九疇使之，並下獄，降廣東參政。

translations.literal: Heng said that Qi and the Right Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuxiu had incited them; both were imprisoned and demoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng said Luo Qi and Right Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuxiu had incited them; both were imprisoned and demoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 綺鞅鞅未赴。

translations.literal: Qi was discontented and did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi was discontented and did not take up his post.

sentences.zh: 明年閏二月，綺鄉人告磁州同知龍約自京還，與綺言天子仍寵宦官，刻香木為王振形以葬。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the following year, a fellow townsman reported that the subprefect of Cizhou, Long Yue, returning from the capital, had told Qi that the emperor still favored eunuchs and had carved fragrant wood in Wang Zhen likeness for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of the following year, a townsman reported that Cizhou Subprefect Long Yue, returning from the capital, had told Luo Qi that the emperor still favored eunuchs and had carved fragrant wood in Wang Zhen likeness for burial.

sentences.zh: 綺微笑云：「朝廷失政，致吾輩降黜。

translations.literal: Qi smiled and said: The court has lost proper governance, causing men like us to be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi smiled and said: The court has lost proper governance, causing men like us to be demoted.

sentences.zh: 」奏上，捕綺下吏，坐死。

translations.literal: When the report was submitted, Qi was arrested and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne, Luo Qi was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，陳所籍財賄于文華門示百官。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated, and the confiscated wealth and bribes were displayed at Wenhua Gate for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: His household was confiscated, and the seized wealth was displayed at Wenhua Gate for officials.

sentences.zh: 家屬戍邊，婦女沒入浣衣局。

translations.literal: His family was banished to the frontier, and the women were sent to the laundry bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His family was banished to the frontier, and the women were sent to the laundry bureau.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，赦為民，還其資產。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was pardoned and restored to commoner status, and his assets were returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was pardoned, restored to commoner status, and his assets returned.

sentences.zh: 時與綺先後鎮四川者，張固，字公正，新喻人。

translations.literal: At the time, one who had earlier garrisoned Sichuan together with Qi was Zhang Gu, style name Gongzheng, a native of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: One who had earlier garrisoned Sichuan around the same time as Luo Qi was Zhang Gu, whose style name was Gongzheng, from Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eighth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 正統初，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was appointed supervising secretary in the Penal Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong he was appointed supervising secretary in the Penal Section.

sentences.zh: 改吏科，奉命撫裕州流民。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Personnel Section and ordered to pacify displaced people in Yuzhou.
